topic: Frugal Tokens: Exploring Cost and Usage Across Coding Agents

competitors.title: Frugal Tokens (dpclark4) — official repo, README, .env.example, docs/harnesses.md
key_points: Local, read-only view of token usage and reported cost in OpenCode, Claude Code, PI, Codex, and Cursor sessions
Requires Deno 2.9+; install via `curl -fsSL https://deno.land/install.sh | sh`
Setup: `cp .env.example .env`, then `deno task build && deno task start`, open http://localhost:9000
Override session locations and API port via .env (PORT, OPENCODE_DB_PATH, CLAUDE_CODE_PROJECT_PATH, PI_SESSION_DIR, CODEX_SESSION_DIR, CURSOR_CHATS_PATH)
Optional FRUGAL_TOKENS_SYNC_INTERVAL_SECONDS for periodic re-import; unset/0 = boot-only sync
Dev mode: `deno task dev` on port 5273 (computes its own API port, ignores PORT)
Read-only access — never mutates agent databases; Cursor capture sidecar is append-only

stats.fact: Frugal Tokens requires Deno 2.9+ and runs locally, serving a read-only web view at localhost:9000
Frugal Tokens supports at least 5 harnesses: OpenCode, Claude Code, PI (Apple), Codex, and Cursor
Setup is two commands after installing Deno: `cp .env.example .env` then `deno task build && deno task start`
OpenCode stores data in SQLite at ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db (OPENCODE_DB_PATH); schema observed July 10, 2026 with OpenCode 1.17.x
Claude Code stores JSONL transcripts at ~/.claude/projects/<encoded-cwd> (CLAUDE_CODE_PROJECT_PATH); version observed Claude Code 2.1.202
Cursor stores per-agent SQLite at ~/.cursor/chats/<workspace>/<agent>/store.db (CURSOR_CHATS_PATH); Cursor does not persist historical token usage or dollar cost in its chat stores
Claude Code transcripts do not report dollar cost, so reportedCost is absent; Frugal Tokens applies versioned model rate cards to emit computedCost
Claude usage maps: input_tokens→uncachedInput, cache_read_input_tokens→cacheRead, cache_creation_input_tokens→cacheWrite, output_tokens→output
Frugal Tokens derives freshPrompt (New input) = input + reported cache write, and processed (Total activity) = input + cache read + cache write + output + reasoning
A single TTL cache miss (responding ~1.5 hours later) cost $6 for one message in a Fable session, per an HN user on the Frugal Tokens thread
Many users have 'no idea how many cache misses were happening' after stepping away for an hour or more — idle gaps invalidate prompt caches and inflate cost
Frugal Tokens appeared as Show HN with 37 points on 2026-08-19 (author dpc94)

angles: Step-by-step local setup: install Deno, copy .env.example, build, start, open localhost:9000 — a complete how-to for the first 10 minutes
Mapping each harness's storage path to .env variables so users can point Frugal Tokens at their actual agent data (OpenCode SQLite, Claude Code JSONL, Codex sessions, PI sessions, Cursor chats)
The hidden cost of prompt-cache misses — idle gaps and TTL expiry turn cheap cache reads into full-priced uncached input; how to spot them in the per-session explorer
Reading the per-session explorer: turn-by-turn token/cost breakdown, cache-miss pricing, and where cost spikes correlate with idle gaps
Cross-harness comparison as a workflow: the same task burns different tokens in OpenCode vs Claude Code vs Codex vs Cursor; independent verification beats vendor claims
Understanding the cache fields: uncachedInput vs cacheRead vs cacheWrite, and how freshPrompt/processed are derived from them
Local-first, read-only privacy angle: no code leaves the machine, no cloud dependency, safe for sensitive codebases
ROI governance angle: as companies tighten budgets after a year of unchecked agent spend, per-session cost diagnostics become a governance requirement
Cache-frugality as a workflow lever: redesign prompts/tooling to cut recurring cost once you can see cache misses
